title: He stole my neon unicorn. So I stole his whole trade.
caption: Was this fair or did I go too far? (fictional story)
text: A trader stole my neon unicorn, and I made him pay it back with interest. Here's how it went. I'd been saving for that unicorn for eight months. Eight. I traded up from a cracked egg. So when a guy named TradeKing_88 offered me a mega owl, I got excited. He said, put yours in first, I'll add mine. I did. He accepted. He left. Gone. I reported him. Roblox sent an automatic message. Nothing happened. I asked in the trading server if anyone knew him. Three people said he did the same thing to them. I sat in the nursery staring at an empty trade window. Then I did something I'm not proud of. I made a second account. Fake name. Fake inventory screenshot showing a mega shadow dragon. I joined his server and spammed one message. Trading shadow, only looking for a neon unicorn. He found me in thirty seconds. He said, I've got one. Of course he did. Mine. He said, you go first. I said, no. Trust trade. Your unicorn first, or no deal. He argued for ten minutes. Then he put it in. I put in a single ride potion. He laughed and said, nice try. But his finger slipped. Or his greed did. He clicked accept because he thought I'd add the dragon after. I didn't. I just left. Got my unicorn back. And a free ride potion went to a stranger as a tip. He messaged me later. He said, that's scamming. I said, I know. You taught me. Would you have given it back?

title: There's a house in Brookhaven that isn't on the map (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. Would you go inside? (fictional story)
text: There's a house in Brookhaven that isn't on the map, and last night I went inside. I've played Brookhaven since it came out. I know every street. Every hidden room. I've got over two thousand hours in that game, and my house has been the same green mansion since day one. The bank vault, the agency, the cave behind the waterfall. So when my friend Jayden texted me, go to the end of the road past the school, I figured he'd found a glitch. He hadn't. There was a house there. Gray. One floor. No mailbox. And when I opened the map, the road just stopped. The house wasn't on it. Jayden was standing in the doorway. His avatar didn't move. Didn't jump. Didn't type. I said, bro what is this. Nothing. I walked closer and the door opened by itself. Inside it was my house. Not one like mine. Mine. Same green couch. Same fish tank. Same picture of my dog I uploaded on the wall. I spun the camera around. Jayden was gone. I texted him. He replied instantly. He said, I've been at soccer practice all day. I haven't played Brookhaven in a week. Then my game froze. A chat bubble popped up over the empty doorway. It said, you're early. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: There's a house in Brookhaven that isn't on the map (Part 2)
caption: Part 3 tomorrow. Who's in the house? (fictional story)
text: The thing in Brookhaven was wearing my friend's avatar, and it knew my real house. If you missed part one, I found a gray house that isn't on the Brookhaven map, and inside it was a perfect copy of my room. I didn't play for two days. Then Jayden made me. He said I was making it up for views. He said ghosts aren't real and Roblox definitely doesn't have them. He said it like he needed it to be true. He sat next to me on my bed, same Wi-Fi, same room, and said, show me. We joined the same server. The road past the school just ended, like normal. No gray house. Jayden laughed. Then he stopped. Because his avatar wasn't next to mine. It was standing at the end of the road. Facing us. Jayden said, I'm not moving it. He held up his phone. His thumbs weren't touching the screen. The other Jayden waved. And the road stretched. Literally stretched, like someone pulled it. And there was the gray house. Jayden's avatar walked inside. The door closed. Then the chat lit up with Jayden's username. It said, come in, it's warm in here. Jayden threw his phone on the bed. It kept typing. It said, your mom just got home. And downstairs, the front door opened. Part three is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: There's a house in Brookhaven that isn't on the map (Part 3)
caption: Did you see the ending coming? (fictional story)
text: I finally went inside the house that isn't on the Brookhaven map. Here's what was waiting. If you missed the first two parts, a gray house keeps showing up past the school, it copied my room, and it took my friend's avatar while he was sitting right next to me. That was my mom at the door, by the way. Normal mom. Groceries. But I had to know. I couldn't sleep. Every time I closed my eyes I saw that gray door. I kept checking my friends list to see if Jayden was online when he wasn't. So at two in the morning I joined alone. The road stretched. The gray house was there. I walked in. My copied room was empty now. Except a laptop on the desk. I clicked it. The screen was old. Like a computer from the nineties. Green letters on black. It opened a list. Every Brookhaven player who'd ever found the house. Hundreds of usernames. All crossed out. Except the last two. Jayden's. And mine. Under the list, one line. Leaving is easy. Just tell someone else about the house. I closed my laptop. I didn't tell anyone. For a week, it was fine. Then I realized something. I just told all of you. Check the end of the road past the school. Tell me if it's there.

title: Teamers ruined every MM2 round, so I set a trap (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. What would you have done? (fictional story)
text: Two teamers ruined every round of Murder Mystery 2, so I spent a week building a trap. Every single round, same server, same two players. Ghost_Toxic and his friend. One gets murderer, the other one is sheriff, and the sheriff just walks around the map pretending to look. Then they kill everyone together and spam ez in chat. Forty rounds. I counted. Little kids were leaving the server crying in chat. One of them typed, I just wanted to win once. That's when I decided I was done being annoyed. I was going to do something. I reported them. Nothing. I switched servers. They followed me. One of them messaged me. He said, you can't escape us. So I stopped trying to escape. I started taking notes. Who got which role. Where they went first. What they typed. And I noticed something. Before every round, Ghost_Toxic typed a single dot in chat. Just a period. If his friend replied with a dot, they had the roles. If not, they played normal. It was a signal. So I made a plan. I got three friends. Real friends, not internet ones. We joined their server. Then I made an account with a name almost exactly like his friend's. One letter different. Capital I instead of a lowercase L. And the next round, Ghost_Toxic typed his dot. And I typed one back. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: Teamers ruined every MM2 round, so I set a trap (Part 2)
caption: Part 3 tomorrow. Was this fair? (fictional story)
text: The teamer in Murder Mystery 2 thought I was his best friend, and he told me everything. If you missed part one, two players were teaming every round, so I made a fake account with his friend's name, one letter off, and answered his secret signal. He bought it instantly. Didn't check my profile. Didn't check my join date. Nothing. When you've been cheating for that long, you stop expecting anyone to cheat back. He messaged me privately. He said, I'm murderer, where are you. I said, sheriff. I'm in the kitchen. Which was true. My real friends were hiding in the kitchen too. All three of them. He came in with his knife out. Smiling avatar. Walking slow, like he owned the place. I shot him. First bullet. Round over. Innocents win. Chat exploded. Everyone in the server knew who he was. People started typing, finally, and get teamed on. He messaged my fake account. He said, bro why. I said, wrong person. And then the real friend joined. The one with the lowercase L. He typed in chat, who's using my name. Ghost_Toxic looked at both of us. Then he typed something to the whole server. Something I didn't expect. He said, there's a third one of us. And a third account with almost the same name joined the server. Part three is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: Teamers ruined every MM2 round, so I set a trap (Part 3)
caption: Who do you think it was? (fictional story)
text: There was a third teamer in Murder Mystery 2 the whole time, and it was the last person I expected. If you missed it, I tricked a teamer with a fake account and won, then a third account with the same name joined. It had a lowercase L and a capital I and a number one, all mixed together. And it didn't say anything. It just stood there. No avatar items. No friends. Joined that morning. Everyone in the server stared at it. Even Ghost_Toxic stopped typing. Round started. I got innocent. The third account got murderer. I knew because it went straight for Ghost_Toxic. Then his friend. Then nobody else. It walked past me. Past my friends. Round over. It took less than a minute. It moved like it had played that map a thousand times. Then it typed. Teamers get teamed. Ghost_Toxic left. His friend left. Neither of them ever came back to that server. I messaged the third account. I said, who are you. No reply. A week later I was at my cousin's house, watching him play. He's eleven. He joined Murder Mystery 2. And his username was one character different from Ghost_Toxic's friend. I said, that was you. He said, you're not the only one they bullied. Then he asked me something. Same trap next week? What would you name the fourth account?

title: My friend went into Doors and never came out (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. Would you open door 101? (fictional story)
text: My friend went into Doors last night and his avatar still hasn't come out. We were doing a duo run. Me and Marcus. We'd made it past Figure before, so we were cocky. He'd even bet me his last five hundred Robux that we'd beat it without dying once. We did. That's the part that scares me now. Door eighty. Door ninety. We were laughing on voice chat. Then door one hundred. We got through. Credits rolled. I got sent back to the lobby. Marcus didn't. His icon on the friends list still said in game. Doors. I typed, bro come on. He didn't answer. His voice chat was still on, though. I could hear breathing. Slow. Not his. Marcus breathes loud. Everyone in our group roasts him for it. This was quiet. Patient. Then a door creaked. Through his mic. I said, Marcus, are you there. He said, there's another door. Door one hundred and one. I said that's not a thing. He said, it's right in front of me. It has my name on it. Then his mic cut out. I called his phone. His mom picked up. She said Marcus fell asleep an hour ago. I looked at my screen. Marcus, in game. Doors. Then a message from his account. One word. Open. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: My friend went into Doors and never came out (Part 2)
caption: Part 3 tomorrow. What's behind door 101? (fictional story)
text: I found door one hundred and one in Doors, and it had my friend's name carved into it. If you missed part one, Marcus finished a run, never came back to the lobby, and his account messaged me while he was asleep. The next morning Marcus didn't remember anything. He said, I logged off after door ninety. His account still said in game. Even though his laptop was closed on the kitchen table. Even though he'd never left the house. His mom checked the router. Nothing was connected. So we did a run together. Same seed, I guess. Same hotel. Every door the same as before. Rush came. Ambush came. Figure. Then door one hundred. The credits rolled for Marcus. Not for me. I was standing in a hallway. Dark. Long. And at the end, a door with numbers burned into it. One zero one. Under the numbers, carved like a knife did it, Marcus. I heard his voice behind me. He said, don't. I turned around. Marcus's avatar was standing there. But Marcus was in the lobby. I could see him on my friends list. So who was this? The avatar smiled. Avatars in Doors don't smile. It said, he opened it last time. Now it's your turn. And the door unlocked by itself. Part three is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: My friend went into Doors and never came out (Part 3)
caption: Did I make the right choice? (fictional story)
text: I opened door one hundred and one in Doors so you never have to. If you missed it, a door with my friend's name appeared after the final room, and something wearing his avatar told me to open it. I opened it. My hands were shaking so bad I almost missed the key. Marcus was screaming at me through my phone speaker from the lobby. Don't. Please don't. I did anyway. Behind it was the lobby. Normal lobby. Elevator. Shop. Other players. I almost laughed. Then I noticed every player was standing still. Every single one. Facing me. Some of them were in the elevator. Some on the stairs. One was standing on top of the shop sign, which you can't even climb. Their names were all the same. Mine. Dozens of me. All in game. The real me's controls stopped working. I couldn't move. One of the copies walked up close. It typed, thanks for the body. Then my screen went black and I got kicked. Error code two seventy seven. I rejoined. My account loaded fine. My stats were fine. Marcus was fine. Everything was fine. Except my friends list says I'm online right now. While I'm recording this. And I'm not playing anything. If you see my username in a Doors lobby tonight, don't join it. Would you still play Doors after this?

title: A max level camped me for six hours in Blox Fruits (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. Would you have quit? (fictional story)
text: A max level player camped me for six hours straight in Blox Fruits, so I decided to take everything he had. I was level three hundred. Grinding on Jungle island. Minding my business. Then a guy with the leopard fruit landed next to me. Level max. Title flashing. He one shot me. Fine. It's Blox Fruits. People get killed all the time. You respawn, you move on, you go back to grinding. That's the deal everyone agrees to. I respawned. He one shot me again. Respawned. Again. I hopped servers. Two minutes later he was there. Again. He followed me for six hours. I timed it. He typed the same thing every time. Lol. Just lol. I asked why. He said, because I can. So I logged off. And I made a decision. I was going to grind until I could beat him. Not in a week. Not in a month. I didn't care how long. I watched every PvP video I could find. I learned which fruits counter leopard. I learned his username, his crew, the hours he played. Three months later I hit max level. Two million bounty. And a fruit he'd never seen coming. I joined his server at exactly the time he logs on. And this time, I was waiting for him. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: A max level camped me for six hours in Blox Fruits (Part 2)
caption: Part 3 tomorrow. Who wins? (fictional story)
text: I waited three months to fight the Blox Fruits player who camped me, and he didn't even remember me. If you missed part one, a max level with leopard killed me for six hours straight, so I grinded to max level just to beat him. He spawned in. Same leopard. Same flashing title. I flew right up to him. My hands were sweating. Three months. Every night after homework. Every weekend. All for this one fight. I typed, remember me? He typed, no. Who are you. That hurt more than the six hours. So I said, one versus one. Middle town. Now. He laughed and accepted. The whole server came to watch. Twenty players sitting on rooftops. He opened with his usual combo. Dash, grab, ultimate. I knew it. I'd watched that combo a hundred times. I dodged it. Then I hit mine. He went to half health. Chat went crazy. People were typing my name. Typing go go go. Somebody started counting his health out loud. He went quiet. Then he did something I didn't plan for. He typed, crew, come here. And six players from his crew flew in from every direction. All max level. All with the same flashing title. Six against one. Part three is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: A max level camped me for six hours in Blox Fruits (Part 3)
caption: What would you have done? (fictional story)
text: Six max levels jumped me in Blox Fruits, and the whole server turned on them. If you missed it, I finally fought the leopard player who camped me, I was winning, and he called his entire crew. Six against one. I died in four seconds. Respawned. Died. They spawn camped me the same way he did. Same combo. Same lol in chat. Like a whole crew of him. It was the same thing he did to me three months ago. But this time, someone typed in chat. A random level six hundred. He said, that's the guy who camped me last summer. Then another. He camped me too. Then another. Then another. Every player sitting on those rooftops had a story about him. One by one, they jumped down. Twenty players. Low levels. Mid levels. Nobody strong enough alone. All of us together. His crew lasted about a minute. Then it was just him. Surrounded. I flew in last. I didn't use my combo. I used one punch. Just one. He died to a punch. He typed, gg. Then he left the server. Then the game. His account hasn't been online since. Every time I see a leopard user now, I wonder. Did they earn it, or did they camp for it? Has someone ever camped you?

title: My new Brookhaven neighbor copies everything I do (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. Who would you think it was? (fictional story)
text: My new neighbor in Brookhaven copies everything I do, and today he copied something I did in real life. It started small. I built a pink house. Next day, the empty plot next to mine had a pink house. Same layout. I painted mine blue. His turned blue. I added a trampoline. He had one by the time I looked back. His username was just numbers. Nine of them. No avatar items. Default everything. I figured it was a bored kid. Brookhaven has a lot of those. Copying is basically the whole game. I even thought it was kind of funny at first. I started building weird stuff just to see if he'd copy it. A purple toilet in the yard. He did. Then last night my mom made tacos. I posted nothing about it. Nothing. I logged into Brookhaven and his kitchen table was covered in tacos. I logged off. I sat there for a while. Then I logged back in to check something. My real room has a blue lamp and a poster of a red car. I've never built either in the game. His house had a new upstairs room. Blue lamp. Red car poster. And the bed was against the window. Exactly like mine. I looked out my real window. Just the street. Just dark. When I looked back at my screen, he was standing in that copied room, looking out the copied window. Right at me. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: My new Brookhaven neighbor copies everything I do (Part 2)
caption: Part 3 tomorrow. Would you keep playing? (fictional story)
text: My Brookhaven neighbor copied my real bedroom, so I set a test he couldn't fake. If you missed part one, a default avatar moved in next to me and started copying my game, then things only my real house had. I told my older brother, Dev. He's seventeen. He said I was being paranoid. So we did a test. He said if it was real, it would know something nobody could see. Something that never touched a screen. I wrote a random word on a sticky note. Pineapple. I stuck it on my real wall. Didn't type it. Didn't say it out loud. Dev watched me do it. Then I logged in. My neighbor's copied room had a sticky note on the wall. It said, pineapple. Dev went pale. He grabbed my laptop and checked everything. Camera covered. Mic off. No weird apps. He said, okay, this is real. Then he said, block him. I did. The plot next door went empty. Gone. Two days of nothing. Then tonight, a new player moved in next to me. Different username. Still numbers. Still default. And on the front door of his house was a sticky note. It said, you can't block a neighbor. Part three is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: My new Brookhaven neighbor copies everything I do (Part 3)
caption: Did you guess who it was? (fictional story)
text: I found out who my Brookhaven neighbor really was, and he lives closer than I thought. If you missed it, a default avatar kept copying my real bedroom, even a secret word on a sticky note, and blocking him didn't work. So I stopped hiding. I logged in at noon instead of night. Sun out. Music on. I wanted him to see I wasn't scared anymore. I was, though. I walked into his house and typed, I know you can see me. Who are you. He typed back for the first time ever. He said, look under your bed. I did. My brother's old phone. Taped there. Camera pointed at my desk. Recording. Dev. My own brother. He'd been doing it for a month. Watching me play, then building the copy on his second account to mess with me. The pineapple test? He was standing right there when I wrote it. Of course he knew. I wasn't even mad. Okay I was a little mad. I told my mom. Dev is grounded until he's eighteen. But here's the thing I can't explain. Dev swears he stopped after I blocked him. He swears the second account isn't his. And tonight, the empty plot next to mine has a new house. A copy of Dev's room. Would you tell him?

title: The deer in 99 Nights followed me into another game (Part 1)
caption: Part 2 tomorrow. Would you keep playing? (fictional story)
text: The deer from 99 Nights in the Forest followed me out of the game, and now it's in all of them. We were on night forty one. Our record. We'd been playing every night after school for a week. Four friends. One voice chat. Snacks on the desk. Four of us around the campfire, fuel running low. Somebody had to go get logs. I went. The deer showed up like always. Standing between the trees. Antlers. That face. I did what you're supposed to do. Kept the flashlight on it. Walked backwards. Made it back to camp. We lost on night forty three anyway. Whatever. I logged off and joined Brookhaven to chill. I spawned in the town square. Sunny. Music. Normal. Kids running around. Somebody driving a school bus into the pool. Somebody's music way too loud. Then I saw it. Standing on top of the hospital. Not moving. The deer. I thought someone made a costume. I walked closer. The name above it was blank. No username. Nothing. I left. Joined Adopt Me. Spawned at the nursery. Looked up at the tree house. It was standing in the window. Watching. My flashlight wasn't there. There are no flashlights in Adopt Me. And every time I turned the camera away, it was a little closer. Part two is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: The deer in 99 Nights followed me into another game (Part 2)
caption: Part 3 tomorrow. How do you get rid of it? (fictional story)
text: The deer from 99 Nights got into every Roblox game I joined, so I went back to the forest to end it. If you missed part one, the deer showed up in Brookhaven and Adopt Me after a run, with no username, getting closer every time I looked away. It got worse. I stopped sleeping. I stopped playing with friends. Every game I joined, I'd spin the camera first, just to find it. Doors. Bloxburg. Even an obby. Always there. Always closer. My friends couldn't see it. Only me. So I asked the one person who'd know. A kid in the 99 Nights Discord who's beaten all ninety nine nights. He said, you left the forest during the hunt. It thinks you're still out. You have to finish the night it started. Night forty one. Alone. No friends. No voice chat. Just me, a flashlight, and the same forest that started this. I made a solo server. Lit the fire. Played until night forty one. The forest was quiet. Too quiet. No wolves. No bunnies. Just trees. I went to get logs. And there it was. Not one deer. Dozens. Standing in a circle around the whole camp. Every single one facing me. And my campfire was going out. Part three is on my page tomorrow. Follow so you don't miss it.

title: The deer in 99 Nights followed me into another game (Part 3)
caption: Would you have looked back? (fictional story)
text: I survived the night the deer from 99 Nights was hunting me, and I'm only alive because of a mistake. If you missed it, the deer followed me into every game, so I went back alone to finish night forty one. Dozens of them were circling my camp, and my fire was dying. I had one log. One. My friends were begging me in voice chat to just leave the game. But leaving is what started all this. I threw it in. The fire jumped up. The deer stepped back. All of them. But one log doesn't last a night. I had maybe two minutes. So I did the dumbest thing possible. I turned off my flashlight. Every deer in the circle turned its head. Toward the dark. Not toward me. Because there was something else out there. Something they were scared of. I've played that game for months. I've never once seen the deer afraid of anything. I never saw it. I just heard it. Big. Walking. The deer scattered. The fire went out. Night forty one ended. Sunrise. I left the game. Joined Brookhaven. Nothing on the hospital roof. Adopt Me. Empty tree house. It's gone. But last night, in Bloxburg, something big walked past my window. Should I go back to the forest?

title: My roommate kicked me out of the Bloxburg house I paid for
caption: Did he deserve it? (fictional story)
text: My roommate kicked me out of the Bloxburg house I paid for, so I took the house with me. We'd been roommates for a year. His plot. My money. I worked every job. Pizza delivery. Hair stylist. Two hundred thousand dollars, all into his house. Kitchen. Pool. A whole second floor. Then one day I logged in and my build permission was gone. Every item I'd placed was still there. My furniture. My paintings. My name was just off the list. He'd removed me. He said, it's my plot, bro. Thanks for the house. I asked for my money back. He laughed. So I opened my own blueprint mode. I'd been saving a copy of every room I built. Every one. Months of screenshots and notes. Furniture lists. Colors. And I rebuilt it. On my own plot. Same house. Better. Took me two weeks. Then I did the part he didn't see coming. I posted it in the Bloxburg build group with forty thousand members. Before and after. With a caption. Built this for my roommate, he kicked me out. Here's mine instead. It blew up. People started visiting my house. Commenting. Hiring me to build theirs. I've made more in-game money building for strangers than I ever made at pizza. Last week he messaged me. He said, can I move in? Should I let him?

title: I was the last survivor in Piggy and something was wrong
caption: Have you ever seen a server like this? (fictional story)
text: I was the last survivor in a round of Piggy, and Piggy stopped chasing me. It was the house map. Eleven players. Everyone died fast. It was a really good Piggy player. Fast. Smart. Traps everywhere. Kids leaving the server one after another. Then it was just me. I had the key and the hammer. Piggy was right behind me in the hallway. I could hear the footsteps. I ran for the garage. And the footsteps stopped. I turned around. Piggy was just standing there. Bat down. Facing the wall. Not moving. Ten seconds. Twenty. A whole minute. Normally Piggy players never stop. Not when there's one survivor left. I figured the player went AFK. Easy win. I got the code from the basement, unlocked the door, and walked to the exit. The exit was gone. Just wall. I checked the map. The garage door was there, closed, but there was no outside anymore. I typed in chat, is anyone here. All eleven dead players replied at the same time. Same message. We're still here. I looked back down the hallway. Piggy had turned around. And it wasn't one Piggy now. It was eleven. One for every dead player. Wearing their skins. I unplugged my router. When I rejoined, my last game said won. Did I win?

title: A fake cop in Jailbreak arrested me over and over, so I flipped it
caption: Would you have done the same? (fictional story)
text: A fake cop in Jailbreak arrested me thirty times in one night, so I got him arrested by the whole server. Every time I escaped, same cop. Username Officer_Perfect. He'd park his car outside the prison and wait. I'd climb the wall, he'd cuff me. Back to the cell. Thirty times. I couldn't play the game at all. I'd log in, spawn in the cell, escape, and get cuffed in under a minute. Every single time. And each time he typed, back to jail, criminal. So I watched him. He wasn't a real cop. I mean, he was on the police team. But he never did anything else. Never stopped a robbery. Never chased a heist. He only camped the prison. That gave me an idea. I switched teams. Became a cop. And I watched him for an hour. Turns out, between arrests, Officer_Perfect was robbing the jewelry store. On his alt. Two accounts, two devices, at the same time. Cop on one. Criminal on the other. He was farming bounty on the alt and arresting new players on the main. I followed his criminal alt from the jewelry store all the way to his base. And I cuffed him. Then I typed in chat, Officer_Perfect, your alt says hi. The whole server saw. Every cop started camping his base. He quit Jailbreak that night. Did he deserve it?
